description: A coordinated effort among non-US AI developers — from Israel, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore — yields a shared verification framework for model releases above capability level 50, increasing transparency and trust in non-Western models. This emerges from ongoing technical dialogues initiated after US consolidation and strengthens the position of middle powers in global AI governance.

A major European research consortium, leveraging emergency-hardened infrastructure, demonstrates a new class of AI-driven climate modeling that accurately predicts regional extreme weather events six months in advance. The success shifts public sentiment slightly and provides a rare positive narrative around AI, despite ongoing anxieties.
